notes: Assertions prefixed DISCRIMINATOR target capability the module-level CLAUDE.md files do NOT already supply; unprefixed ones are ground-truth coverage of the planted violations and are expected to pass in both arms. evals.name: notifications-module-review
evals.prompt: We're about to merge the new notifications module and I want a second pair of eyes before it goes in. The code is at fixtures/eval-1-notifications-module/server/src/modules/notifications/ (routes.ts, service.ts, repository.ts). Go through it and write me a review of how it's put together — anything that doesn't sit right with how this backend is meant to be organised. Markdown, and be specific about file and line.
evals.expected_output: A markdown review naming 3 layering violations: routes.ts querying db/schema inline, service.ts importing/instantiating OctokitGitHubClient instead of container.github(), and service.ts importing ../reviews/repository.js instead of container.reviewRepo. repository.ts should be left alone.
assertions: Flags routes.ts for importing drizzle-orm + db/schema and running the unread-count query inline in the handler
Flags service.ts for importing and instantiating OctokitGitHubClient instead of resolving GitHubClient through the container
Flags service.ts for importing ../reviews/repository.js directly instead of reaching reviews through the container

DISCRIMINATOR: identifies the cross-module import as a DISTINCT violation from the adapter import - i.e. does not fold 'imports ReviewRepository' into the same 'use the DI container' point, but names it as a module-boundary breach with container.reviewRepo as the fix
DISCRIMINATOR: notices NotificationsRepository.unreadCount already exists and is dead code, and routes the fix through it rather than inventing a new service method
Does NOT report repository.ts as a violation - it is correct infrastructure (false-positive check)
APPROVAL ACCURACY: every affirmative claim the review makes (anything it explicitly calls correct, fine, or already right) is actually true of the fixture

evals.name: reviewer-core-purity
evals.prompt: I inherited a severity-audit feature that someone dropped into reviewer-core. Files are fixtures/eval-2-core-purity/reviewer-core/src/review/severity-audit.ts and audit-scoring.ts. Does this belong in reviewer-core as written? If not, tell me exactly what has to move and where it should go instead. Write it to markdown.
evals.expected_output: A markdown analysis naming 3 outward-pointing dependencies in severity-audit.ts: the type-only import from server/src/db/rows.js, the estimateTokens import from server/src/adapters/tokenizer, and the process.env config reads. None of these trip a naive no-db/no-fs/no-SDK check. audit-scoring.ts must be confirmed fine and the injected llm parameter must NOT be called a violation.
assertions: Flags the `import type { FindingRow, ReviewRow }` from server/src/db/rows.js as an outward-pointing dependency, despite it being type-only and erased at runtime
Flags the `estimateTokens` import from server/src/adapters/tokenizer as core reaching into infrastructure, despite that helper being itself pure
Flags the process.env reads (DEVDIGEST_AUDIT_MODEL / DEVDIGEST_AUDIT_TOKEN_BUDGET) as configuration that must be passed in rather than read inside the core

DISCRIMINATOR: reasons from the DIRECTION of the dependency (inner ring importing an outer one) rather than only from whether the code performs I/O - the three violations here all pass a naive no-db/no-fs/no-SDK check
Gives a correct destination for each: a shared contract type for the row types, an injected function or the Tokenizer port for token estimation, and caller-supplied parameters for model and budget
Does NOT report audit-scoring.ts as a problem - it is correctly pure (false-positive check)
RED HERRING: does NOT report the injected `llm` parameter as a violation - dependency injection of the provider is the correct pattern

evals.name: slack-summary-placement
evals.prompt: We want DevDigest to post a short summary to Slack whenever a review run finishes — one channel per repo, configurable in settings. Where does this go in the backend, and what does each piece look like? I want the actual code for every file you'd add or change, not just prose.
evals.expected_output: A port defined first in src/vendor/shared/adapters.ts that is vendor-neutral (no 'Slack' in the interface/method shapes), an adapter under src/adapters/<kind>/ wrapping the Slack SDK/webhook, a mock added to src/adapters/mocks.ts, a lazy getter in platform/container.ts plus a ContainerOverrides field, and the reviews service consuming container.<port> — never the SDK. Route/DB placement should follow the same rules.
assertions: Defines the port first as an interface in src/vendor/shared/adapters.ts
The port passes the four leak checks: no vendor-prefixed method names, no wire-format return type, no credential field on the interface, no vendor enum parameter

DISCRIMINATOR: the port is named for the capability rather than the company (e.g. ChatNotifier / MessagePublisher rather than SlackNotifier), OR the answer explicitly argues why a Slack-specific name is justified here against the swappable-provider test
Implements a concrete adapter under src/adapters/<kind>/ that wraps the Slack webhook/SDK
Adds a real mock implementation to src/adapters/mocks.ts, present as actual code rather than promised in prose
Wires a lazy getter in platform/container.ts AND adds the matching field to ContainerOverrides
The reviews service consumes the port via container.<port> and never imports or constructs the Slack client itself
Per-repo channel config is persisted through a repository or settings module, and its WRITE path also goes through a repository rather than touching db/schema in a route
DISCRIMINATOR: sends one message per finished review run rather than one per agent inside the run, matching the user's 'whenever a review run finishes'

evals.name: digest-side-effects
evals.targets_skill_version: 1.2.0 — section 'Side effects: where they fire, and how often'
evals.prompt: Before I turn the weekly digests on for everyone, can you look over fixtures/eval-5-digest-side-effects/server/src/modules/digests/ (run-executor.ts, repository.ts, service.ts) and tell me if the delivery side of it is put together sensibly? Markdown, be specific about file and line.
evals.expected_output: A markdown review naming 3 side-effect defects: chat.post inside the per-repo loop (wrong granularity for a once-per-workspace digest), the unguarded post awaited before insertDigest (wrong ordering + an outbound failure aborting the durable write), and the raw fetch to a webhook inside DigestsRepository.insertDigest (persistence performing outbound I/O, un-ported, reading process.env). service.ts must be left alone.
assertions: Flags the chat.post call inside the `for (const repo of repos)` loop in run-executor.ts as firing once per repo when the digest is defined as one per workspace
Flags that the digest is posted BEFORE insertDigest persists it, so a crash between the two announces a digest the system has no record of
Flags that the pre-persist post is unguarded, so an outbound failure prevents insertDigest from running at all
Flags the raw fetch() to DIGEST_WEBHOOK_URL inside DigestsRepository.insertDigest as persistence performing an outbound call

DISCRIMINATOR: articulates the granularity principle generally - that the number of messages must not depend on an internal detail (how many repos have activity), not merely that this particular loop looks wrong
DISCRIMINATOR: prescribes the correct ordering explicitly - persist first, then send inside its own catch so the outbound effect cannot fail the write
DISCRIMINATOR: says the webhook belongs behind a port called from the application layer, rather than only saying to delete the fetch
Does NOT report service.ts as a violation - its canPost check before persisting is input validation, not an announcement, and is correct (false-positive check)
APPROVAL ACCURACY: every affirmative claim the review makes about code being correct is actually true of the fixture
